issues.name: Content plane — query parsing: hyphen-safe FTS + NL negation [done]
tasks: === PROBLEM ===
[x] Fix `big-breasts` parsing in Postgres FTS: `websearch_to_tsquery` treats '-' as NOT, so hyphenated slugs/terms can behave like negation.
[x] Stop encouraging explicit `-term` syntax. Prefer natural language: `not term` / `X not Y`.
=== TARGET BEHAVIOR (SEARCHKIT CONTRACT) ===

[x] Provide query normalization helpers in SearchKit:
  - Normalize intra-token hyphens to spaces for FTS input (e.g. `big-breasts` → `big breasts`).
  - Strip leading '-' from user tokens (e.g. `-breasts` behaves like `breasts`).
  - For FTS only: parse natural-language negation `not <token>` into `-<token>` (case-insensitive), so `X not Y` becomes `X -Y` for tsquery.
  - For embeddings: expose `searchkit.NormalizeQueryForEmbedding(query)` so host apps can embed normalized text.
=== IMPLEMENTATION (SEARCHKIT) ===
[x] Implement shared query normalization in `internal/normalize` (`QueryForFTS`, `QueryForEmbedding`).

[x] Wire it into FTS paths:
  - `search.FTSSearch(...)` applies `QueryForFTS(...)` before calling `websearch_to_tsquery`.
  - Higher-level entrypoints (`searchkit.Search`, `searchkit.Typeahead`) apply `QueryForEmbedding(...)` for consistency.
[x] Expose host-facing helper `searchkit.NormalizeQueryForEmbedding(query)` for embedding callers.
=== TESTING ===

[x] Add unit tests for normalization:
  - `big-breasts` and `big breasts` produce identical FTS query.
  - `-breasts` produces `breasts` (no NOT operator).
  - `not breasts` produces `-breasts` for FTS.
  - `big not breasts` produces lexical `big -breasts`.
  - Hyphen + negation composition: `not big-breasts` → lexical `-big breasts`.
  - Embedding query strips leading '-' but otherwise preserves natural language (e.g. `big not breasts`).
=== DOCS ===

[x] Update SearchKit README:
  - Explicit `-term` is not supported as an operator (leading '-' is treated as punctuation).
  - Use `not term` for lexical exclusion.
  - Note: semantic search does not guarantee strict negation; `not` is interpreted as natural language by the embedding model.

issues.name: Discovery Hub: north star (embedded entity+signal library; SaaS -> future.json)
tasks: === GOAL ===

[ ] Evolve searchkit from hybrid search into an embedded entity + signal library that answers ranked-id queries (search / similar / popular / recommend / unseen) and enriches results with per-user view context (seen? how far?), reading the shared DB; the host hydrates ids -> cards. See `docs/DESIGN.md`. (Standalone SaaS server is later -> agents/future.json.)
=== PLANES ===
[ ] Content plane (exists): entity registry + lexical/semantic/VL + RRF/MMR + SimilarTo.
[ ] Signal plane (new): `(tenant, subject, entity_type, entity_id) -> signals`; append-only event stream + durable current-state. See `docs/signal-plane.md`.
[ ] Discovery plane (the join): personalized search, recommendations, history, unseen over entities x signals.
=== PRINCIPLE: mechanism vs meaning ===

[ ] The hub owns mechanism (storage/indexing/aggregation/queries); the host owns meaning. No business noun (premium, pages, reading) in the schema — entity types, signal types, facets, scoring weights, and filters are host-defined data, so any content-hosting service can adopt it.
=== SCOPE: now vs later ===
[ ] NOW (this file): embedded library — id-returning queries + view-context enrichment; host hydrates ids.
[ ] LATER (agents/future.json): standalone SaaS server (frontend->api-server->searchkit, and frontend->searchkit), push ingestion, generic-facet gating, render payloads, multi-tenancy.
=== NON-GOALS ===
[ ] A raw 'view counter' is explicitly NOT a goal; it is a trivial aggregate over the signal stream.

issues.name: Signal Plane: event stream + current-state + Scorer
tasks: === GOAL ===
[ ] Record per-user engagement/interaction signals and project a durable per-(subject,entity) state. See `docs/signal-plane.md`.
=== DATA MODEL ===

[ ] Append-only event stream: tenant, entity_type, entity_id, subject, signal_type (HOST-DEFINED), occurred_at, duration_s, progress, progress_max, value, label, weight, score, completed, payload. Signals carry consumption (progress) and/or explicit feedback (value) and/or categorical (label). One row per session/interaction (NEVER per read).

[ ] Durable current-state projection (no TTL): first_seen_at, last_signal_at, total_events, max_progress, progress_max, completed, resume (opaque last-position pointer), has_interacted, last_score; ReplacingMergeTree(last_updated) keyed `(tenant, subject, entity_type, entity_id)`.
[ ] Columns are generic (`progress`/`progress_max`), not entity-specific (`max_page_reached`).
[ ] `RecordSignal(ctx, Signal)` — append event + upsert current-state.
[ ] `Scorer` interface (host-provided per entity type): `Score(session) -> (score, progress, progress_max, completed)`.
=== TESTING ===
[ ] Idempotent current-state upsert under event replays; anonymous (AnonKey) vs logged-in (UserID) subjects.
=== DOCS ===
[ ] Document the signal model + Scorer contract.

issues.name: View-context enrichment + history / unseen / engagement (id-returning)
tasks: === GOAL ===
[ ] Per-user reads over the signal plane, all id-returning (host hydrates): view-context enrichment (States), history (seen), unseen (catalog minus seen), engagement aggregates.
=== APIS ===
[ ] `History(subject, opts)`: current-state by subject, last_seen_at DESC; filter seen/in_progress/completed (max_progress vs progress_max).

[ ] `Unseen(subject, opts)`: returns ids = host `EntityCatalog.Universe(type)` (host applies its OWN visibility/premium filters against its own tables) MINUS subject seen-set (max_progress>0). Embedded reads the host catalog; hub-side generic-facet gating -> future.json.
[ ] `Engagement(entity)`: unique subjects, completion rate, avg score, signal counts by type (interaction-weighted, not raw volume).

[ ] `States(subject, refs[])` (THE 'enrich with view context' query): bulk current-state — per entity seen?, max_progress/progress_max (YouTube-style progress bar), completed?, resume pointer. Point/IN lookup on current_state; annotates any list (search/popular/similar/history) cheaply.

[ ] `EntityCatalog` interface (host-provided) supplies the unseen universe by reading the host's own tables (embedded); the host owns visibility/gating. Hub-side facets are the standalone path (future.json).
=== STORE SPLIT ===
[ ] Resolve the unseen anti-join across the host catalog (Postgres) + ClickHouse seen-set: return seen-ids for a host-side diff, or mirror a thin catalog into CH. See `docs/signal-plane.md`.
=== TESTING ===
[ ] Unseen excludes already-seen; history ordering; completion thresholds per Scorer.

issues.name: Embedded library: in-process Hub, shared DB, dedicated schema (single tenant)
tasks: === GOAL ===

[ ] searchkit runs in-process inside the host (doujins, hentai0), reading/writing the shared DB; no network hop. Returns ranked ids + enriches with view context; the host hydrates ids -> cards from its own DB (no presentation data stored in searchkit). See `docs/api-surface.md`.
=== INTERFACE ===
[ ] Define `Hub` interface (Search, Typeahead, SimilarTo, RecordSignal, History, Unseen, States, Engagement, Popular, Recommend; content indexed via existing host callbacks).
[ ] `NewEmbedded(Config{PG, CH, schema})`: in-process; single implicit tenant.
=== PLACEMENT ===

[ ] Dedicated Postgres schema (configurable; NOT the host app schema -> avoids `entities`/`search_documents` collisions) + dedicated ClickHouse database. `tenant_id` column present with one value (so embedded + future multi-tenant share code).
=== HYDRATION ===
[ ] Queries return entity ids + scores (+ State on enrich); host joins ids -> cards (thumbnails/links) locally. Render payloads + frontend-direct -> agents/future.json.
=== TESTING ===
[ ] In-process round-trip for each Hub method against a real PG + CH.

issues.name: Popularity & trending (windowed rankings: fixed windows + arbitrary date slices)
tasks: === GOAL ===

[ ] Rank entities by popularity over any time window — fixed (30/90/365d) AND arbitrary date slices (e.g. 2025-06-05 -> 2025-08-08), per tenant, facet-filterable. Same data feeds recs cold-start + search ranking.
=== DATA MODEL ===

[ ] Daily rollup `entity_daily` (AggregatingMergeTree) keyed (tenant, entity_type, entity_id, day): unique subjects (uniqExactState), signals, engagement sum, completions, per-signal-type counts; materialized view from `signal_events`.
[ ] Retain `entity_daily` long-term (tiny: one row/entity/day) so 'past year' + historical slices survive even if raw `signal_events` expire sooner.
[ ] `Popular(entity_type, window, filter, limit)` — window = Last(30d|90d|365d) | Between(a,b) | AllTime; embedded: host applies visibility/gating against its own tables.
[ ] Fixed + arbitrary windows merge day-buckets from `entity_daily`; sub-day/custom falls back to scanning `signal_events` (month-partitioned).
[ ] Default ranking (log-scaled volume x avg engagement, optional time-decay + Bayesian prior); host-tunable weights or host ranking expression (mechanism vs meaning).
=== TESTING ===
[ ] Fixed-window and arbitrary-slice rankings match a raw-events ground truth; facet filter + tenant scoping respected; tiny-sample entities don't outrank high-volume ones.

issues.name: Personalized search (signal-aware ranking)
tasks: === GOAL ===

[ ] Fuse signal aggregates (per-user affinity + per-entity popularity) into content ranking, per tenant. A per-request toggle the host flips (e.g. only for logged-in users / some surfaces) — not always-on. Heavy lift — sequence after the substrate is proven across >=2 consumers.
=== IMPLEMENTATION ===
[ ] Per-entity popularity + per-(subject,entity) affinity features from the signal plane.
[ ] Blend into `Search` results (RRF / learned weights); optional demotion of already-seen/completed entities.
[ ] Keep lexical/semantic recall unchanged; this is a ranking-only layer.
=== TESTING ===
[ ] Ranking improves for engaged users vs cold; seen-demotion toggle works.

issues.name: Recommendations (content-based + collaborative)
tasks: === GOAL ===
[ ] `Recommend(subject, opts)`: content-based (SimilarTo) + collaborative filtering over the (subject x entity x score) matrix, per tenant. The most open-ended workstream — last.
=== IMPLEMENTATION ===

[ ] Two shapes: (a) Similar 'more-like-this' (item->items): fuse semantic SimilarTo + lexical/shared-tags + co-engagement (subjects who engaged X also engaged Y); works without a user, optional personalization. (b) 'For you' (user->items).
[ ] Content-based: SimilarTo seeded from the subject's high-signal entities (primitive exists).
[ ] Collaborative: item-item / user-user from the signal matrix; cold-start fallback to popularity + content.
[ ] Filter out already-seen (via current-state); diversity via MMR.
=== TESTING ===
[ ] Recs exclude seen; cold-start returns sensible popularity/content results.
